notes: PSA 9 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.18. Prostate volume 49 mL. csPCa 0.80.

note_sections.t: An upward PSA trajectory combined with a previously positive biopsy necessitates specialist re-evaluation.

A 57-year-old retired carpenter initially came under investigation three years ago due to elevated PSA levels. He is married and occupies an independent unit within a neighborhood retirement community, with his adult son designated as the primary contact. Tobacco use consists of a 17 pack-year history, discontinued in 2021. Lower urinary tract symptoms remain minimal, reflected by an IPSS score of 1 out of 35. Physical activity includes tennis twice weekly, while alcohol intake stays around two units per week. Past surgical history includes a laparoscopic cholecystectomy in 2018 and bilateral cataract extraction in 2022. Routine dermatological surveillance for actinic keratosis and a planned gastroenterology colonoscopy both returned unremarkable results. An Arabic interpreter has been secured for this consultation. He currently takes no regular medications and has no other comorbidities.

DRE: The prostate presents as symmetrically enlarged with smooth, firm parenchyma and absolutely no discrete nodules or asymmetry. General inspection shows a well-nourished individual in no acute distress; cardiovascular and respiratory examinations yield normal results. Vital parameters remain stable, recording a blood pressure of 115/79 mmHg and a regular heart rate of 80 bpm.
